Foreword
There’s a saying in software: “ It works on my machine.” But cloud-native architecture asks a better
question: “ Does it work for everyone, everywhere, all the time? ”
That’s the bar now. We’re not just pushing code—we’re designing systems. Living, breathing
systems that scale globally, survive outages, secure data by default, and adapt to change before
we even see it coming. And doing all that? That takes more than clever code—it takes architecture.
Cloud-native architecture.
Stéphane Eyskens has done something important here. He hasn’t just written a book full of ref -
erence diagrams or dense documentation. He’s mapped the terrain. He’s created a guidebook for
real-world, production-ready architecture on Azure—one that acknowledges the complexity but
still invites you in with clarity, structure, and (yes) some humility.
What I appreciate most about this mapbook is that it doesn’t pretend cloud-native design is one-
size-fits-all. It respects the nuance: the trade-offs, the roles, the business pressures, the difference
between “ it deploys ” and “ it endures.” It teaches the craft without gatekeeping it. And the hands-on
exercises? They meet you where you are, while nudging you toward where you need to be.
Whether you’re a developer who’s become architecture-curious, an architect who wants to go
deeper into Azure-native tooling, or a leader looking to design solutions that don’t just survive
but thrive, this book has something for you.
So go ahead. Read this mapbook. Dog-ear it. Build with it. Break things (in test). Learn. Grow.
Because this cloud? It’s native now. And this is how we architect it—on purpose, with care, and
with the kind of practical wisdom that Stephane has generously packaged into every page.
Scott Hanselman
Vice President, Developer Community, Microsoft
Contributors
About the author
Stéphane Eyskens has a developer background and became a solution architect about a decade
ago. As a cloud subject matter expert, he contributed to many digital transformation programs,
helping organizations get better results out of their cloud investments. As an MVP, he is an active
contributor to the Microsoft Tech Community and has worked on multiple open source projects
available on GitHub. Stéphane is also a Pluralsight assessment author as well as the author of
multiple books and online recordings.
I wish to express my deepest gratitude to my reviewers, Massimo Crippa and George Chrysovalantis
Grammatikos, for their invaluable insights, rigor, and generosity. Their thoughtful feedback helped shape
this book into a far clearer, stronger, and more balanced work. I am equally grateful to my wife, whose creative
touch brought clarity to the architectural maps that accompany this book. Lastly, I’d like to thank Preet Ahuja

Georgios-Chrysovalantis Grammatikos is a cloud integrator discipline sublead and senior
Azure cloud architect at Node4. He was recognized in 2025 as a Microsoft MVP in two areas: Azure
and Business Applications. With over 15 years of experience in the cloud industry and more than
7 years specializing in architecture and consultancy, his primary focus includes cloud technology,
security, and artificial intelligence. George enjoys sharing his knowledge. He actively participates
in the Microsoft Learn community and other technology groups. As an international speaker, he
enjoys taking part in and organizing events. He has also helped review several books and blogs.
I want to express my appreciation to Stéphane Eyskens, the author of The Azure Cloud Native Architecture
Mapbook, Second Edition, for picking me as one of the technical reviewers for this edition. Additionally, I
appreciate his readiness to cooperate on revisions and improvements to the content, ensuring the best possible
experience for readers. Lastly, I thank Arun Nadar, content engineer at Packt, for his support throughout
the book review process.
Massimo Crippa is a cloud solution architect and Microsoft Azure MVP with over 20 years of
experience designing and delivering enterprise solutions on Microsoft technologies. He began his
career as a web developer, later moving into middleware and messaging solutions before focusing
on helping organizations modernize and move to the cloud. Today, Massimo works across the
full cloud journey, from defining strategy and showcasing Azure PaaS, serverless, and container
solutions, to delivering hands-on implementations that drive business impact. A passionate
advocate for innovation and cloud-native thinking, Massimo is dedicated to helping organiza -
tions embrace a tech-intensive mindset. When he’s not architecting solutions, he’s a proud dad,
motorbike enthusiast, and lifelong learner exploring the evolving world of the cloud.

Preface
Writing about Azure is a humbling experience. The platform evolves faster than any single book
could ever hope to capture in full. New services appear, existing ones merge or fade, and best prac -
tices constantly shift. Yet beneath this flux lies something enduring—the architectural principles,
mental models, and trade-offs that shape every successful Azure solution.
This book was written to uncover that enduring layer. It doesn’t aim to document every feature
or service in detail; Microsoft’s documentation already does that brilliantly. Instead, it seeks to
give you a map—a way to navigate Azure’s vastness with purpose and clarity. Whether you are
an architect defining a cloud strategy or an engineer implementing complex workloads, you’ll
find here the reasoning, patterns, and structure to make informed choices in the Azure ecosystem.
The journey begins with foundational thinking about what it means to architect in the cloud and
how different roles contribute to that process. It then dives progressively into each vertical, such
as infrastructure, containers, data, development, security, and artificial intelligence. Each chapter
balances conceptual depth with practical insight, offering a cohesive narrative that connects the
dots between technology, governance, and enterprise-grade practices.
Throughout, the emphasis is on why—why one architecture pattern fits better than another,
why certain Azure services align naturally with specific goals, and why trade-offs must always
be made. Real-world pragmatism anchors every discussion, because architecture ultimately lives
in the tension between ideals and constraints.
Think of this book as a compass, not an encyclopedia. It won’t give you all the answers—but it
will help you ask the right questions. It will help you reason through design decisions, foresee
implications, and approach Azure not as a collection of tools, but as a coherent ecosystem.
If you come away with a clearer sense of direction, a stronger architectural mindset, and renewed
curiosity to explore further, then this book will have fulfilled its purpose.
Preface xvi
Who this book is for
This book is for cloud architects, engineers, and technical decision-makers who design, build, or
govern solutions on Azure. It assumes a solid grasp of cloud and architecture fundamentals but
welcomes readers from all backgrounds—whether you specialize in infrastructure, development,
data, or security. It’s not only about Azure; it’s about connecting the dots across architecture
disciplines, showing how they come together to form cohesive, cloud-native solutions. If you’re

Part 1
Building the Foundations
Part 1 lays the groundwork for becoming an effective Azure architect by connecting cloud fun -
damentals with practical design disciplines. It introduces the key architectural roles and mind -
sets, then progressively expands from broad solution architecture concepts to the infrastructure
and platform layers that bring them to life. You will explore the essential Azure building blocks,
network topologies, and operational foundations such as backup, high availability, and disaster
recovery. The section also dives into the container ecosystem—examining Azure Kubernetes
Service in depth, including multi-tenant and service mesh patterns, and comparing it with other
container options to help architects choose the right balance between control, complexity, and
agility. Altogether, these chapters establish a solid foundation for designing and operating scal -
able, secure, and well-governed Azure solutions.
This part of the book includes the following chapters:
• Chapter 1, Getting Started as an Azure Architect
• Chapter 2, Solution Architecture
• Chapter 3, Infrastructure Design
• Chapter 4, Working with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
• Chapter 5, Working with Other Container Services
• Chapter 6, Developing and Designing Applications with Azure
1
Getting Started as an Azure
Architect
In this chapter, we will focus on what an architect’s role entails and explain the various cloud
service models that are made available by the Microsoft Azure platform. We will describe how

90652.title: azurecloudnativearchitecturemapbooksecondedition
90652.heading: Chapter 10, Closing Thoughts and Next Steps, provides a summary of the entire book as well as useful
90652.content:
the numerous maps in this book are built, what they intend to demonstrate, and how to make
sense of them.
More specifically, in this chapter, we will cover the following topics:
• Getting to know architectural duties
• Getting started with the essential cloud vocabulary
• Introducing Azure architecture maps
• Understanding the key factors of a successful cloud journey
Our purpose is to help you learn the required vocabulary that is used across the book. You will
also understand the duties of an Azure architect. We will explain the most frequently used service
models and their typical associated use cases, which every Azure architect should know. We start
smoothly, but be aware that the level of complexity will increase as we go. Let’s start by getting
acquainted with the definition of an architect.
